41725068.model_family: computer vision workflow with clustering, classification, and event-based modeling (open-source machine learning algorithms)
41725068.clinical_problem: predicting CNS vasculopathy / stroke risk in sickle cell anemia from MRA vessel morphology
41725068.patient_population: children with sickle cell anemia enrolled in a completed clinical trial who underwent brain MRA
41725068.model_description: An automated computer vision workflow extracts quantitative vessel morphology metrics (including small-vessel features not captured by conventional scoring) from pediatric brain MRA. Open-source machine learning methods then cluster scans, classify them by clinical risk group, and order vascular features by an event-based model of relative change, to explore associations between vessel remodeling/tortuosity and stroke risk.
41725068.release_evidence: applied open-source machine learning algorithms, including: clustering... classification... event-based modeling
41725068.study_design: retrospective analysis of clinical-trial neuroimaging data using unsupervised and supervised machine learning

41727682.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in children with rare growth/endocrine/lysosomal storage disorders
41727682.patient_population: 1,138 hand radiographs from multiple centers, children with SHOX deficiency, Noonan syndrome, Silver-Russell syndrome, Turner syndrome, pseudohypoparathyroidism, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, precocious puberty, mucopolysaccharidosis I/II/III/IV/VI, alpha-mannosidosis and unclassified lysosomal storage disorders
41727682.model_description: Deeplasia is an open-source deep learning system that estimates bone age from a hand radiograph using the Greulich and Pyle method. It was externally validated against a mean of 2-5 expert human raters on radiographs from children with rare syndromic, endocrine, and lysosomal storage disorders.
41727682.headline_result: MAE 5.95 months (cohort 1, endocrine/syndromic) and 7.13 months (cohort 2, lysosomal storage disorders); 1-year accuracy 89.9% and 81.2% respectively; outperformed all individual human raters

41727769.body_region: thoracic spine (T1, T7, T12 vertebrae) on chest radiograph
41727769.clinical_problem: assessing correct positioning of tubes and catheter tips relative to thoracic vertebral landmarks in critically ill newborns
41727769.patient_population: 14,660 neonatal chest radiographs from 10 university hospitals in Korea, including infants with and without tubes/catheters
41727769.model_description: A fully automated nnU-Net-based deep learning system segments and labels the T1, T7, and T12 thoracic vertebrae on neonatal chest radiographs, to help map anatomical target regions for assessing tube and catheter tip positioning in the NICU.
41727769.dataset_size: 14,660 neonatal chest radiographs (11,860 training, 1,400 validation, 1,400 test)
41727769.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient 0.83 (T1), 0.83 (T7), 0.80 (T12); >90% localization accuracy at DSC threshold 0.5-0.6
41727769.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and validation

41736619.body_region: fetal head / maternal pelvis (intrapartum transperineal ultrasound)
41736619.clinical_problem: automating measurement of fetal head position (Angle of Progression) to assess labor progression
41736619.patient_population: women in labor undergoing transperineal intrapartum ultrasound at Kaplan Medical Center
41736619.model_description: A fully automated deep learning algorithm analyzes transperineal intrapartum ultrasound video, automatically identifies optimal frames, and measures the Angle of Progression without manual intervention, to standardize assessment of fetal head descent during labor.
41736619.release_evidence: preliminary results from a system developed at Kaplan Medical Center; no release stated
41736619.study_design: narrative review / single-center technical development, preliminary results

41740276.model_family: hybrid CNN-Transformer (Series-Parallel Large Kernel Attention, Multi-layer Edge-enhanced Perception, Short-range Concatenation Decoding)
41740276.clinical_problem: segmenting necrotizing enterocolitis lesions on abdominal radiographs in neonates
41740276.model_description: NEC-Net is a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture that segments necrotizing enterocolitis lesions on neonatal abdominal radiographs, using attention modules for elongated structures, boundary sensitivity, and small-lesion decoding, to support radiological alerting and clinical deployment.
41740276.release_evidence: The model, along with associated tools, is available at https://github.com/priscillaLee0830/NEC-application

41745445.model_family: fused VGG-19, ResNet-50, MobileNet-V2 CNN features with Chi-Square feature selection and SVM classifier
41745445.clinical_problem: detecting childhood pneumonia on chest radiographs
41745445.patient_population: children imaged with chest radiography for pneumonia diagnosis (publicly available pneumonia CXR dataset)
41745445.model_description: Three pretrained CNNs (VGG-19, ResNet-50, MobileNet-V2) extract features from pediatric chest radiographs; a Chi-Square selection step removes redundant features before fusing subsets from the two best-performing networks, which are then classified as pneumonia or normal using a support vector machine.
41745445.study_design: retrospective technical development on a public benchmark dataset

41747211.clinical_problem: screening for idiopathic scoliosis without radiography
41747211.patient_population: 236 participants aged 8-18 years (154 with idiopathic scoliosis, 82 healthy controls) from 2 reference hospitals in France and Canada
41747211.model_description: A smartphone application captures video scans of a patient's back and uses AI to estimate the major coronal spinal curve from 3D surface topography, without radiation, to screen for idiopathic scoliosis; results were compared, blinded, against standard radiographic curve measurements.
41747211.headline_result: sensitivity 100%, specificity 89% for detecting curve >10 degrees

41750182.model_family: spatially constrained ICA + ComBat harmonization + support vector machine
41750182.clinical_problem: classifying autism spectrum disorder from resting-state fMRI connectivity
41750182.patient_population: multi-site rs-fMRI cohort from ABIDE I and II (children/adults with ASD and healthy controls across 11 sites)
41750182.model_description: A semi-blind independent component analysis identifies functional brain networks from resting-state fMRI, with ComBat harmonization to correct for scanner/site differences across 11 datasets; a support vector machine then classifies ASD versus healthy controls using features from the default mode, sensorimotor, and visual sensory networks.
41750182.dataset_size: multi-site rs-fMRI dataset, 11 independent datasets (ABIDE I and II)
41750182.headline_result: classification accuracy up to 83.23% (visual sensory network, AUC 87.90%)
41750182.study_design: retrospective multi-site machine learning classification study

41753073.clinical_problem: monitoring joint space width / cartilage health after treatment for juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of the knee
41753073.patient_population: 21 skeletally immature patients treated for juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of the distal femur, 2002-2017
41753073.model_description: IB Lab KOALA, a validated AI-based software, automatically measures joint space width on standardized anteroposterior knee radiographs, used here to compare the affected and contralateral knee and across treatment groups (conservative, drilling, fragment refixation) in juvenile osteochondritis dissecans.
41753073.release_evidence: validated AI-based software IB Lab KOALA(TM), Version 2.4
41753073.headline_result: no significant JSW differences between affected/contralateral knee or treatment groups; average JSW >6 mm at median 64-month follow-up
41753073.study_design: retrospective cross-sectional feasibility study with systematic review

41761049.body_region: fetal brain (cavum septum pellucidum et vergae, lateral posterior ventricle horn, choroid plexus, cerebellum, cortical plate)
41761049.clinical_problem: automated segmentation of fetal (sub)cortical brain structures on 3D ultrasound for fetal neuroimaging assessment
41761049.patient_population: 270 3D ultrasound volumes from 141 fetuses, 19-26+6 weeks' gestation, acquired on a different ultrasound vendor than the training data
41761049.model_description: Deep learning models automatically segment five fetal (sub)cortical brain structures on 3D ultrasound volumes. The study evaluates these models on a novel dataset acquired with a different ultrasound vendor, using both the Dice similarity coefficient and a new clinician-focused 4-point visual grading framework.
41761049.headline_result: 87.2% of segmentations graded adequate overall; CSPV/ChP/CBM >90.5% adequate; LPVH lowest at 73.9% adequate

41764315.body_region: brain (multimodal: diffusion tensor imaging, structural MRI, resting-state functional connectivity)
41764315.clinical_problem: predicting socioeconomic status / family income from multimodal brain imaging
41764315.patient_population: children/adolescents with multimodal neuroimaging (DTI, structural MRI, resting-state functional connectivity)
41764315.model_description: Elastic net regression models predict family socioeconomic status, particularly income, from multimodal brain imaging (diffusion tensor imaging, structural MRI, and resting-state functional connectivity), with and without demographic information, to identify which imaging features are most discriminative of SES.
41764315.headline_result: AUC 0.75 (test)/0.811 (train) for income without demographics; AUC 0.81 (test)/0.969 (train) distinguishing top vs bottom income deciles

41769581.clinical_problem: diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip using AI-assisted ultrasound and radiography
41769581.patient_population: infants and children evaluated for developmental dysplasia of the hip (literature review, no single cohort)
41769581.model_description: A literature review summarizing AI applications (deep learning, CNNs, segmentation networks, 3D convolutional models) for automated landmark detection and measurement of the alpha angle, beta angle, and acetabular index on hip ultrasound and radiographs, for diagnosing developmental dysplasia of the hip.

41774084.clinical_problem: predicting neurodevelopmental impairment from brain volume in preterm infants with germinal matrix hemorrhage
41774084.patient_population: 171 preterm infants (<37 weeks gestation) with cranial ultrasound and 3D T1 brain MRI at 34-46 weeks postmenstrual age, December 2020-August 2024
41774084.model_description: A U-Net-based algorithm automatically segments supratentorial and white matter brain volumes from term-equivalent-age 3D T1 MRI in preterm infants, to test whether reduced volume relative to sex-specific norms is associated with germinal matrix hemorrhage grade and later neurodevelopmental impairment (measured by Bayley-III).
41774084.headline_result: supratentorial volume-PMA slope 19.37 cm3/week control vs 12.37 GMH (P=0.02) vs 11.49 PWML (P=0.04); standardized residuals differed significantly between NDI and non-NDI in GMH group (P<0.001)

41775248.clinical_problem: predicting spontaneous preterm birth using AI
41775248.patient_population: pregnant women assessed for preterm birth risk across reviewed studies
41775248.model_description: A narrative review of AI approaches to predicting spontaneous preterm birth, including electronic-health-record models, deep learning analysis of cervical ultrasound images, cervical texture/radiomics feature extraction, elastography-derived parameters, and multi-omics transformer models, evaluating their methodological quality against TRIPOD and risk-of-bias criteria.
41775248.headline_result: AUC range 0.61-0.89 across modalities; 79% of studies at high risk of bias; median TRIPOD adherence 49%

41781648.model_family: lightweight deep neural network (CNN), benchmarked against AlexNet, MobileNet, ResNet18, Xception
41781648.clinical_problem: differentiating autism spectrum disorder from ADHD subtypes (combined, hyperactive/impulsive, inattentive) and neurotypical children
41781648.patient_population: children from the ABIDE and ADHD-200 public datasets
41781648.model_description: ADBrainNet is a lightweight deep neural network trained on resting-state fMRI images to classify five groups: ASD, three ADHD subtypes, and neurotypical children. Explainable-AI (LIME) is used to highlight the imaging features driving each classification.
41781648.headline_result: mean accuracy 61.87% (+/-5.59%), F1 62.50% (+/-5.78%) on independent external test set, five-fold cross-validation
41781648.study_design: retrospective machine learning classification study on public datasets

41787418.body_region: fetal anatomy (first-trimester, biometry, anomaly scan planes)
41787418.clinical_problem: improving fetal ultrasound image quality/standardization in low-resource settings
41787418.patient_population: 61,959 fetal ultrasound examinations (551,144 images) from 186 sonographers at 34 hospitals in Guizhou Province, China, September 2020-May 2025
41787418.model_description: An independent, post-examination AI quality-control system scores each fetal ultrasound image 0-100 and classifies it as standard, basic-standard, or non-standard against national plane-acquisition guidelines, to give sonographers feedback and track image-quality trends over time across a multicenter, multi-county rollout.
41787418.dataset_size: 61,959 examinations (551,144 images) from 186 sonographers at 34 hospitals
41787418.headline_result: full-standard first-trimester scans rose from 39.5% to 82.1%; standard anomaly scans from 16.1% to 53.3% over 36 months (all p<0.0001)

41792516.clinical_problem: forensic skeletal age and sex estimation from hand radiographs for disaster victim identification
41792516.patient_population: 13,865 hand radiographs from the RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge and Roboflow HandBone datasets, ages 0-19 years, tested on 200 hold-out samples
41792516.model_description: A two-stage deep learning system first uses YOLOv8x to detect 17 anatomical keypoints and segment 19 bones on a hand radiograph, then an EfficientNet-B0 stage estimates biological age and sex from these skeletal features, independent of soft tissue, for forensic identification.
41792516.headline_result: age MAE 7.75 months, R2 0.942, ICC 0.993; sex classification accuracy 94% (kappa 0.88)
41792516.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation on public datasets

41793451.clinical_problem: differentiating medulloblastoma from pilocytic astrocytoma preoperatively in children
41793451.patient_population: 113 children with medulloblastoma and 74 with pilocytic astrocytoma
41793451.model_description: A multimodal MRI radiomics model extracts features from DCE-T1WI, T2WI, and ADC sequences and combines them into a radiomics nomogram to distinguish medulloblastoma from pilocytic astrocytoma before surgery in children with posterior fossa tumors.

41807430.clinical_problem: generalizable segmentation of brain tumors (including pediatric gliomas) across diverse patient populations
41807430.patient_population: five tumor populations: adult gliomas, pediatric gliomas, Sub-Saharan African gliomas, intracranial meningiomas, and brain metastases
41807430.model_description: MTSS-KDNet distills the knowledge of several population-specific teacher segmentation models (including one trained on pediatric gliomas) into a single unified student model, using latent- and output-level supervision, so that one MRI brain tumor segmentation model generalizes across adult, pediatric, and other tumor populations without separate models.
41807430.headline_result: average Dice 0.87 (whole tumor), 0.84 (tumor core), 0.77 (enhancing tumor) across all five populations, outperforming population-specific models

41807718.clinical_problem: automating fetal cardiac function assessment on echocardiography
41807718.patient_population: internal dataset of 52,942 annotated images from 1,940 normal fetal echocardiograms; external testing on 245 normal echocardiograms and 83 abnormal echocardiograms
41807718.model_description: A fully automated AI workflow detects and segments fetal cardiac structures on echocardiogram images, performs quality control, then calculates cardiac function parameters, referenced to a dynamic gestational-age Z-score model, replacing labor-intensive manual measurement.
41807718.dataset_size: 52,942 images from 1,940 normal fetal echocardiograms (internal); 245 normal + 83 abnormal echocardiograms (external)
41807718.headline_result: mean Dice similarity coefficient >92%, mean IoU >85% across all test datasets; lower variability than manual or Fetal HQ measurement

41811458.clinical_problem: reviewing AI applications across pediatric abdominal imaging tasks (detection, classification, functional analysis, severity prediction, segmentation, image-quality optimization, acquisition acceleration)
41811458.model_description: A clinically oriented review, organized by organ, of published AI research in pediatric abdominal imaging, covering detection, classification, functional analysis, severity prediction, automated segmentation, image-quality optimization, and acquisition acceleration; it notes that most pediatric AI research so far has focused on musculoskeletal rather than abdominal imaging and that most applications remain confined to the research setting.

41813681.model_family: EfficientNetB0 and InceptionV3 CNNs (compared to SVM baseline)
41813681.clinical_problem: distinguishing acute bilirubin encephalopathy from non-ABE hyperbilirubinemia in neonates
41813681.patient_population: 150 neonates (75 with ABE, 75 with hyperbilirubinemia without ABE)
41813681.model_description: A computer-aided diagnosis system feeds T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and ADC brain MRI (individually and fused) into convolutional neural networks (EfficientNetB0, InceptionV3) to distinguish neonates with acute bilirubin encephalopathy from those with hyperbilirubinemia but no encephalopathy, whose MRI findings can otherwise look similar.
41813681.headline_result: best model (InceptionV3, fused T1/T2/ADC) accuracy 0.9622, AUC 0.9978, F1 0.9617

41819797.clinical_problem: noninvasively predicting BRAF mutation status (fusion vs V600E vs non-BRAF) in pediatric low-grade glioma to guide targeted therapy
41819797.patient_population: 511 children with pediatric low-grade glioma and known BRAF status, presurgical MRI, two institutions, January 2009-January 2023
41819797.model_description: Radiomics features are extracted from manually segmented tumors on multisequence presurgical MRI (FLAIR, T2WI, contrast-enhanced T1WI, ADC); random forest classifiers combining clinical and radiomics features predict three-class BRAF mutation status (fusion, V600E, non-BRAF) in pediatric low-grade glioma, to help select candidates for molecularly targeted treatment when biopsy is not feasible.
41819797.dataset_size: 511 children (223 BRAF fusion, 105 BRAF V600E, 172 non-BRAF); 180 with all 4 MRI sequences
41819797.headline_result: best single sequence FLAIR macro-AUC 0.82; multisequence ensemble/concatenation macro-AUC 0.79

41824048.clinical_problem: estimating gestational age from fetal brain imaging when last menstrual period/ultrasound biometry is unreliable, particularly in late pregnancy
41824048.patient_population: 1,321 fetal MRI scans for training/evaluation; 80 additional publicly available fetal MRI scans as an external test set
41824048.model_description: Deep learning models (transfer-learned ResNet-101, compared against training from scratch and single- vs multi-view input) predict gestational age from multi-view fetal brain MRI; explainability analysis showed the model attends mainly to the lateral ventricles and cerebellum.
41824048.dataset_size: 1,321 fetal MRI scans (internal); 80 public MRI scans (external test set)
41824048.headline_result: internal test MAE 4.47 days, R2 0.96; external test MAE 6.57 days vs 9.42 days for biometric regression
41824048.study_design: retrospective model development with external validation

41825499.model_family: multi-instance learning (deep learning) combined with clinical features
41825499.clinical_problem: distinguishing strangulated from simple small bowel obstruction in children on CT
41825499.patient_population: 168 hospitalized pediatric patients aged 1-14 years with small bowel obstruction, January 2018-June 2024, multicenter
41825499.model_description: A deep learning multi-instance learning (MIL) model analyzes abdominal CT images and is combined with clinical features to discriminate strangulated from simple small bowel obstruction in children; SHAP values explain feature contributions, and the model is tested as decision support for radiologists and surgeons.
41825499.headline_result: combined model AUC 0.87 (95% CI 0.72-1.00) in external test cohort; MIL assistance increased physician AUC by 2-20 percentage points
41825499.study_design: retrospective multicenter diagnostic model development and validation

41827281.clinical_problem: estimating the postmortem interval in fetal death for forensic purposes
41827281.patient_population: 94 fetuses >=20 weeks' gestation after feticide (63 retrospective training, 28 prospective validation)
41827281.model_description: A gradient boosting machine model, built with automated machine learning, predicts the postmortem interval of a fetus from 3D postmortem ultrasound measurements of corneal and ocular volume (cornea-to-eyeball ratio), for forensic use; a web application was built to deploy the model.
41827281.release_evidence: A Shiny web application was developed to facilitate clinical implementation (no URL or open-source statement given)
41827281.headline_result: training R2 0.91 (RMSE 11.49h, MAE 8.45h); validation R2 0.75 (RMSE 18.32h, MAE 14.49h)
41827281.study_design: single-center model development with prospective validation cohort

41827957.clinical_problem: shortening emergency pediatric brain MRI while preserving diagnostic image quality
41827957.patient_population: pediatric emergency brain MRI cases (case series), including leukoencephalopathy in ALL, brain abscess, diffuse axonal injury, posterior circulation infarction, leukostasis syndrome, and posterior fossa tumor with hydrocephalus
41827957.model_description: Two vendor deep-learning-accelerated MRI protocols, GOBrain (3D volumetric encoding, compressed sensing, DL reconstruction) and Deep Resolve Swift Brain (multi-shot EPI with DL reconstruction), are demonstrated on a series of pediatric emergency brain cases to produce a multi-contrast diagnostic brain MRI in minutes.
41827957.release_evidence: GOBrain and Deep Resolve Swift Brain, developed by Siemens Healthineers

41838099.model_family: random forest (ensemble) and L2-penalized logistic regression radiomics
41838099.clinical_problem: detecting effects of prenatal alcohol exposure on fetal liver development
41838099.patient_population: 21 fetal MRIs with prenatal alcohol exposure and 45 without, gestational age matched
41838099.model_description: Texture-based radiomics features from fetal liver MRI are used to train random forest and L2-penalized logistic regression classifiers to try to discriminate fetuses with prenatal alcohol exposure from those without, alongside manual liver volumetry.
41838099.headline_result: ROC-AUC 0.43 (random forest), 0.40 (logistic regression) - radiomics could not discriminate exposure status; no significant difference in liver volume or signal intensity

41838340.clinical_problem: reviewing radiomics applications for fetal brain development assessment, malformation phenotyping, and outcome prediction
41838340.model_description: A narrative review of fetal brain MRI radiomics, covering technical foundations (acquisition, segmentation, feature extraction, machine learning models) and clinical applications: brain development phenotyping, Chiari II malformation/edema, isolated ventriculomegaly persistence, and neurodevelopmental outcome prediction.

41844700.clinical_problem: noninvasive quantification of liver fat (MASLD) in obese children
41844700.patient_population: 40 pediatric patients (age 12.16+/-2.56 years) referred for suspected MASLD
41844700.model_description: Two AI approaches -- an XGBoost radiomics model and a deep learning model (Mod-MHDNet) -- use ultrasound radiofrequency data, attenuation parameters, and clinical variables to estimate pediatric liver fat fraction, benchmarked against MRI-PDFF as the reference standard.
41844700.headline_result: R2 = 0.81 (XGBoost) and 0.76 (Mod-MHDNet) vs MRI-PDFF; mean bias <0.4 percentage points

41845248.model_family: LASSO-selected ultrasound radiomics + logistic regression nomogram
41845248.clinical_problem: predicting placenta accreta spectrum in women with placenta previa
41845248.patient_population: 271 pregnant women with placenta previa from two centers in China (190 training, 81 external validation)
41845248.model_description: Radiomic features from gray-scale prenatal ultrasound images of the placenta are selected by LASSO and combined with the number of prior cesarean deliveries in a logistic regression nomogram to predict placenta accreta spectrum in women with placenta previa.
41845248.study_design: retrospective two-center model development with external validation

41845255.model_family: multivariable logistic regression (planned); machine learning as secondary analysis
41845255.clinical_problem: predicting postnatal circulation outcome in fetuses with pulmonary atresia/critical pulmonary stenosis with intact ventricular septum, for counseling and intervention selection
41845255.patient_population: non-intervened fetuses diagnosed with PA/CS-IVS between 16+0 and 28+6 weeks' gestation, international cohort, retrospective (from 2013) plus prospective validation
41845255.model_description: Study protocol for an international cohort that will use standardized prenatal and postnatal fetal echocardiographic data to build a multivariable logistic-regression prognostic model (with a planned machine-learning secondary analysis) predicting postnatal circulation outcome in fetuses with pulmonary atresia/critical pulmonary stenosis with intact ventricular septum.
41845255.study_design: protocol for an international observational cohort study with prospective external validation

41850496.model_family: automated brain volumetry + machine-learning-style feature selection with logistic regression
41850496.body_region: brain (limbic structures: amygdala, hippocampus, nucleus accumbens)
41850496.clinical_problem: identifying structural brain correlates of language delay in late-preterm children
41850496.patient_population: 151 late-preterm children (31 with language delay, 120 without), T1-weighted MRI at term-equivalent age
41850496.model_description: NeuroQuant, an automated volumetry tool, measures limbic and striatal brain structure volumes from term-equivalent-age T1 MRI in late-preterm infants; exploratory feature selection and logistic regression relate these volumes to later receptive and expressive language delay.
41850496.headline_result: language delay associated with increased left amygdalar volume and decreased hippocampal volume

41851784.model_family: cascaded dual-transfer learning (TEN-S: transfer EfficientNetV2; TY-PS: transfer YOLOv11)
41851784.clinical_problem: screening for ductal-dependent congenital heart disease and differentiating critical subtypes (coarctation of aorta, interrupted aortic arch, transposition of great arteries) on fetal echocardiography
41851784.patient_population: 9,142 fetal aortic arch echocardiographic long-axis view images and 58 ultrasound clips from three medical institutions
41851784.model_description: TLEUDS is a cascaded dual-transfer-learning system for fetal echocardiography: a first module (TEN-S, based on EfficientNetV2) screens for ductal-dependent congenital heart disease, and a second module (TY-PS, based on YOLOv11) further classifies critical subtypes (coarctation of the aorta, interrupted aortic arch, transposition of the great arteries), designed to handle variable image quality across sites.
41851784.dataset_size: 9,142 fetal aortic arch images and 58 ultrasound clips from three institutions
41851784.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and validation

41861366.model_family: deep learning (HRNet-based) with pixel intensity data transformation
41861366.clinical_problem: automating Cobb angle measurement and severity classification for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis across multiple hospitals
41861366.patient_population: 3,899 full-spine radiographs from 7 hospitals (2 in Hong Kong, 5 in Mainland China), January 2012-August 2024
41861366.model_description: SpineHRNet+ is a deep learning model that predicts Cobb angle and scoliosis severity from full-spine radiographs; this study adds a real-time pixel-intensity data transformation step to standardize contrast/brightness across scanners and hospitals, improving robustness when applied to radiographs from centers outside the training sites.
41861366.dataset_size: 3,899 radiographs from 7 hospitals (3,034 training/internal validation, 865 external validation)
41861366.headline_result: mean Cobb angle prediction error within 4 degrees (SD 3.12 degrees), R2 >0.90 across all centers; sensitivity 90.18%, negative predictive value 93.16% for severity grading
41861366.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation

41868687.clinical_problem: detecting pediatric lymphoma lesions on whole-body PET/MRI
41868687.patient_population: 53 pediatric lymphoma patients for training, 30 additional scans for testing
41868687.model_description: A convolutional neural network is trained on annotated whole-body [18F]FDG-PET/MRI scans from pediatric lymphoma patients to detect lesions across five anatomical regions, and its sensitivity, specificity, and reading time are compared with a pediatric radiologist and a radiology resident.
41868687.headline_result: CNN sensitivity 84.6%, specificity 93.7% (vs resident 69.2%/81.5%, vs pediatric radiologist 98.7%/99.5%); median read time 4 min (CNN) vs 8 min (radiologist) vs 15 min (resident)

41870581.clinical_problem: preoperative identification of a ventrally positioned right hepatic artery in children with congenital biliary dilatation, to reduce surgical risk
41870581.patient_population: 232 patients with congenital biliary dilatation (116 with ventrally positioned right hepatic artery, 116 controls), single center
41870581.model_description: A YOLOv12-based model trained on radiologist-selected key arterial-phase CT slices detects a ventrally positioned right hepatic artery, a surgically important anatomic variant, in children with congenital biliary dilatation, and is compared against two radiologists.
41870581.headline_result: best sub-model (YOLOv12n) recall 0.842, F1 0.914, mAP50 0.989, AUC 0.977; outperformed junior radiologist (AUC 0.737, P<0.001), comparable to senior radiologist (AUC 0.947, P=0.515)
41870581.study_design: retrospective single-center model development and reader comparison

41870933.clinical_problem: enabling real-time autonomous ultrasound image segmentation (e.g. prenatal fetal biometry, bladder/urinary retention monitoring) on wearable, battery-powered devices
41870933.patient_population: bladder and fetal head ultrasound segmentation datasets (not further specified)
41870933.model_description: A custom 28nm chip implements a binarized U-Net with 4-bit skip connections for on-device, real-time medical image segmentation in wearable ultrasound patches, validated on bladder and fetal head segmentation datasets, aiming to preserve accuracy while eliminating external memory and cutting energy use for battery-powered, privacy-preserving deployment.
41870933.headline_result: 13.4 frames per second, 23 microJ per frame on bladder and fetal head segmentation datasets

41874983.model_family: self-supervised contrastive learning (dual spatial/temporal contrastive loss)
41874983.clinical_problem: objectively detecting fetal movement from ultrasound video to assess prenatal health
41874983.patient_population: 92 subjects, each with 30-minute extended fetal ultrasound video recordings
41874983.model_description: CURL is a self-supervised contrastive learning framework that learns motion representations from extended obstetric ultrasound video recordings, using a dual spatial-temporal contrastive loss and a task-specific sampling strategy, to detect fetal movement without relying on maternal perception or cardiotocography.
41874983.release_evidence: Our code is available at: https://github.com/Mr-TalhaIlyas/CURL/
41874983.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study

41875851.body_region: brain (multimodal neurocritical care biosignals including MRI)
41875851.clinical_problem: prognosis, monitoring, and future pediatric applications of multimodal AI in neurocritical care, including neuroimaging-based neuroprognostication
41875851.patient_population: pediatric and neonatal neurocritical care patients (literature review)
41875851.model_description: A review of AI/machine-learning approaches that fuse multimodal neurocritical-care biosignals (hemodynamic waveforms, intracranial pressure, EEG, near-infrared spectroscopy, neuroimaging, and EHR data) for monitoring and prognosis, with examples including MRI-based neuroprognostication in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, and a discussion of validation and implementation priorities for pediatric translation.

41876706.model_family: multivariate brain-based predictive machine learning models
41876706.body_region: brain (cortical thickness, surface area, gray matter volume)
41876706.clinical_problem: identifying neuroanatomical correlates of impulsivity in youth
41876706.patient_population: Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study participants at baseline (n=8630), 2-year (n=5998), 4-year (n=4844), and 6-year (n=3100) follow-up
41876706.model_description: Multivariate brain-based predictive models use regional cortical thickness, surface area, and gray matter volume from structural MRI to predict self-reported impulsivity measures in a large, longitudinal youth cohort, examining consistency across sexes and developmental timepoints.

41880886.clinical_problem: classifying and triaging pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures (Gartland system) into operative versus non-operative management in the emergency department
41880886.patient_population: 1,811 annotated AP/lateral radiographs from a single tertiary pediatric orthopedic center, 2010-2017; tested on 215 independent radiograph pairs
41880886.model_description: A convolutional neural network trained with transfer learning classifies pediatric elbow radiographs into operative (Gartland IIB, III, flexion type) versus non-operative supracondylar humerus fracture categories, to support emergency-department triage where specialist orthopedic input may not be immediately available.
41880886.headline_result: accuracy 77% (95% CI 71-82%), AUROC 0.84 (95% CI 0.78-0.89); kappa vs surgeon consensus 0.51

41888253.clinical_problem: early diagnosis of necrotizing enterocolitis from deep-learning-derived features on neonatal abdominal radiographs
41888253.model_description: A letter to the editor discussing the implications and next steps of deep-learning-derived features on neonatal abdominal radiographs for early diagnosis of necrotizing enterocolitis, commenting on a prior study.

41888281.model_family: dual-stream deep learning (EfficientNet + MLP with Feature-wise Linear Modulation)
41888281.clinical_problem: predicting pulmonary function impairment (FVC/FEV1 abnormality) from spinal deformity in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
41888281.patient_population: 178 patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis undergoing preoperative standing posteroanterior radiography and pulmonary function testing
41888281.model_description: A dual-stream deep learning model combines an EfficientNet backbone reading standing spine radiographs with a multilayer perceptron processing structured clinical data, fused via Feature-wise Linear Modulation, to jointly predict abnormal forced vital capacity and FEV1 in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis before surgery.
41888281.headline_result: macro-AUC 0.827 (FVC AUC 0.814, FEV1 AUC 0.841), outperforming logistic regression on tabular features (macro AUC ~0.71)
41888281.study_design: retrospective model development study, five-fold cross-validation

41890593.clinical_problem: early detection and intervention planning for neurodevelopmental disorders (autism, ADHD, genetic/metabolic syndromes, cerebral palsy, developmental delay) using MRI
41890593.patient_population: children with suspected or diagnosed neurodevelopmental disorders (literature review)
41890593.model_description: A review of pediatric MRI approaches (diffusion imaging, quantitative MRI, resting-state fMRI, spectroscopy) combined with machine learning and integrative genomics for early biomarker-based detection and risk stratification of neurodevelopmental disorders.

41890888.model_family: deep learning automated segmentation + classification pipeline
41890888.clinical_problem: staging Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (modified Waldenstrom system) from hip radiographs
41890888.patient_population: 2,164 images from institution 1 for training/hold-out testing; external validation at institution 2 (533 radiograph pairs); patients with confirmed LCPD at two tertiary children's hospitals
41890888.model_description: A deep-learning pipeline automatically segments the femoral epiphysis on paired AP and frog-lateral hip radiographs, extracts quantifiable epiphyseal parameters (e.g., sclerosis, epiphyseal area), and classifies modified Waldenstrom stage of Legg-Calve-Perthes disease, evaluated for both early-vs-late staging and full staging.
41890888.headline_result: hold-out AUROC 0.82 (early vs late); external validation AUROC 0.75; segmentation Dice 0.93
41890888.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and external validation

41892913.model_family: vision-language model + multimodal large language model with retrieval-augmented generation
41892913.clinical_problem: generating interpretable, evidence-based diagnoses from pediatric chest radiographs
41892913.patient_population: VinDr-PCXR public pediatric chest radiograph dataset
41892913.model_description: A two-stage system: a vision-language model fine-tuned on pediatric data first extracts structured radiological findings from a chest radiograph, then a multimodal large language model combines the image, extracted findings, patient demographics, and retrieved external medical knowledge to generate a final diagnosis, aiming to mirror radiologists' evidence-based reasoning rather than a black-box classification.
41892913.headline_result: 90.1% diagnostic accuracy, 70.9% F1-score, 82.5% AUC; up to 13.1% accuracy improvement over baselines
41892913.study_design: retrospective technical development on a public benchmark dataset

41899807.clinical_problem: quantifying normal craniofacial growth and sexual dimorphism patterns across childhood and adolescence to guide orthodontic/maxillofacial treatment timing
41899807.patient_population: 41,625 individuals aged 4-18 years, lateral cephalometric radiographs
41899807.model_description: An end-to-end deep learning model, trained without manual landmark annotation, learns imaging features on lateral cephalometric radiographs associated with continuous age and sex; Grad-CAM saliency maps and two new indices (Age-related and Sex-related Saliency Index) quantify which craniofacial bone regions drive age- and sex-related appearance changes during growth.
41899807.study_design: retrospective large-scale deep learning development study

41901651.clinical_problem: screening for hip dysplasia in children with cerebral palsy using AI-analyzed pelvic radiographs
41901651.patient_population: children <=18 years with cerebral palsy undergoing hip surveillance radiographs, across 6 included studies (over 4,000 radiographs)
41901651.model_description: A systematic review comparing AI models against expert clinicians for detecting hip dysplasia (by migration percentage) on pelvic radiographs in children with cerebral palsy undergoing routine hip surveillance.
41901651.headline_result: AI sensitivity 70-97.4%, specificity 85-96%, AUC 0.923-0.999 across 6 studies; only one study externally validated

41902792.model_family: multitask, view-agnostic transformer-based architecture (expands on PanEcho)
41902792.clinical_problem: automated detection of critical and non-critical congenital heart disease on echocardiography, to extend expert-level interpretation to under-resourced settings
41902792.patient_population: internal cohort: 54,727 echocardiograms (3.4 million videos) from Boston Children's Hospital, median age 7.1 years; referral cohort: 3,356 echocardiograms (167,484 videos) from external US and international centers, median age 2.5 years
41902792.model_description: EchoFocus-CHD is a multitask, view-agnostic deep learning model (built on the PanEcho architecture with an added transformer encoder) that detects 12 critical and 8 noncritical congenital heart lesions, individually and as composites, from full pediatric echocardiogram studies, trained and tested internally then evaluated on an independent US/international referral cohort.
41902792.dataset_size: 54,727 echocardiograms internal (3.4M videos); 3,356 echocardiograms referral cohort (167,484 videos)
41902792.headline_result: internal AUROC 0.94 (critical CHD composite), 0.90 (noncritical composite); referral cohort AUROC 0.77 for critical CHD, improving to 0.87 after retraining on all US data
41902792.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development with external referral-cohort validation

41907297.model_family: cross-modal attention transformer with self-supervised contrastive learning + spatiotemporal convolution-LSTM
41907297.clinical_problem: staging fetal lung maturity and individualizing antenatal glucocorticoid dosing
41907297.patient_population: 320 pregnancies (160 with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy), weekly imaging 28-36 weeks' gestation, prospective cohort
41907297.model_description: A physiology-informed multimodal AI framework combines 2D/3D ultrasound, shear-wave elastography, Doppler, and maternal metabolomics, constrained by a placenta-pulmonary coupling model, to unsupervised-stage fetal lung maturity and predict an individualized antenatal glucocorticoid dose and administration window, using a cross-modal attention transformer and a convolution-LSTM dosing branch.
41907297.headline_result: downstream classifier 92.3% accuracy distinguishing early vs late maturity; dosing predicted within +/-0.5 mg of clinical dose, 27% reduction in projected RDS risk vs standard dosing
41907297.study_design: prospective cohort study with multimodal AI framework development

41913353.clinical_problem: clinician attitudes toward AI as a diagnostic aid during fetal anomaly ultrasound
41913353.patient_population: 151 obstetric sonographers, midwives, gynecologists, and fetal medicine consultants in the Netherlands performing fetal ultrasound
41913353.model_description: A survey of Dutch obstetric sonographers and gynecologists on their attitudes, expectations, and concerns about AI applications (already used by 62% of respondents, mainly for automated biometry) as a diagnostic aid during fetal anomaly ultrasound scans.
41913353.headline_result: 62% already use AI (mainly automated biometry); 87% support AI use; 86% want to retain final clinical authority

41914059.clinical_problem: diagnosing adolescent temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis using clinical and imaging predictors
41914059.patient_population: 79 adolescents (10-18 years) with TMJ pain undergoing panoramic radiography and MRI
41914059.model_description: Three decision-tree machine learning models (clinical-only, imaging-only, and combined clinical+imaging) predict temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis in adolescents using panoramic radiograph and MRI findings alongside clinical variables, to identify the strongest diagnostic predictors.
41914059.headline_result: imaging-only model AUROC 0.719; combined model AUROC 0.657 (sensitivity improved to 0.606); panoramic radiograph finding of TMJ-OA was strongest single predictor (OR 3.93)
41914059.study_design: retrospective diagnostic model development study, nested 5-fold cross-validation

41915527.body_region: kidney / urinary tract (renal pelvis and calyces)
41915527.clinical_problem: reconstructing 3D anatomy of congenital hydronephrosis for diagnosis, prognosis, and urodynamic simulation
41915527.patient_population: pediatric patients with congenital hydronephrosis undergoing magnetic resonance urography
41915527.model_description: KidMesh is an end-to-end deep neural network that directly reconstructs a 3D mesh of the hydronephrotic renal collecting system from magnetic resonance urography, without requiring manual mesh-level annotations or external post-processing, enabling downstream urodynamic flow simulation.
41915527.headline_result: reconstruction in 0.4s average; 3.7%/0.2% of vertices with error >3.2mm/6.4mm; Dice 0.86 against manual masks
41915527.study_design: retrospective technical development and validation study
